# Methodology {#sec-methodik}

Describe and justify your methodology. These examples from the V1 templates
show how to integrate, explain, and reference equations.

## Fourier transform and mathematical notation {#sec-fourier}

Equations are part of the text, so punctuation also belongs in displayed
equations. One example is the Fourier transform

$$
\underline{U}(\mathrm{j}\omega)
= \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} u(t)\,\mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{j}\omega t}\,\mathrm{d}t.
$$ {#eq-fourier-transformation}

In @eq-fourier-transformation, $\underline{U}(\mathrm{j}\omega)$ denotes the
Fourier transform of the time-dependent signal $u(t)$. Here, $\omega$ is the
angular frequency and $\mathrm{j}$ is the imaginary unit. Variables in the
running text use the same mathematical typesetting as in the equation.

Physical quantities are italicized; units and mathematical constants are set
upright. In $t = 5\,\mathrm{s}$, $t$ is a quantity and $\mathrm{s}$ is the unit
second. Euler's number $\mathrm{e}$, the imaginary unit $\mathrm{j}$, and the
differential $\mathrm{d}t$ are also upright [@austrianstandards2018].

A comma can connect an equation to the following clause, as in the inverse
Fourier transform

$$
u(t) = \frac{1}{2\pi}
\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}
\underline{U}(\mathrm{j}\omega)\,\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{j}\omega t}\,\mathrm{d}\omega,
$$ {#eq-fourier-invers}

which reconstructs the time-domain signal from its Fourier transform.
Variables that have already been introduced need not be defined again.

## Systems of equations and alignment {#sec-gleichungssysteme}

Several related equations can form one block. @eq-lineares-system shows a
linear system with inputs $x_1$, $x_2$, outputs $y_1$, $y_2$, and coefficients
$A_{ij}$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
y_1 &= A_{11}x_1 + A_{12}x_2, \\
y_2 &= A_{21}x_1 + A_{22}x_2.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-lineares-system}

Equations of different lengths are aligned at the equals sign. In
@eq-spannungen, $U_2$ is the voltage across $R_2$, and $U_{\mathrm{ges}}$ is the
total voltage across the series-connected resistors $R_1$ and $R_2$. The same
current $I_{\mathrm{ges}}$ flows through both resistors.

$$
\begin{aligned}
U_2 &= I_{\mathrm{ges}} R_2, \\
U_{\mathrm{ges}} &= I_{\mathrm{ges}}(R_1 + R_2).
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-spannungen}

## Long equations and sums {#sec-lange-formeln}

Long equations are broken at a meaningful point before they collide with the
equation number or page margin. @eq-logarithmusreihe shows the series
expansion of the natural logarithm with a sum, powers, and several fractions.
The domain $0 < x \leq 2$ is part of the mathematical statement.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\ln(x)
&= \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^{n+1}}{n}(x-1)^n \\
&= (x-1) - \frac{(x-1)^2}{2} + \frac{(x-1)^3}{3} - \cdots, \\
&\qquad 0 < x \leq 2.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-logarithmusreihe}

In Quarto, these examples use LaTeX math. The `aligned` environment
aligns lines at `&`; `\\` starts a new line. Each
related block has one number and one label here. References are updated automatically.
